title: WS-I Basic Profile Version 2.0
note: Requirement statements extracted with wsi_requirements.py. The published document is served through a CDN that rewrites contributor addresses per response, so a digest of the raw HTML is not reproducible; this extract is, and it is what the ledger quotes.

R9999.statement: Any WIDGET SHOULD be round in shape.

R9701.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST be serialized as XML 1.0.

R4006.statement: A RECEIVER MUST support the presence of a UTF-8 Unicode Byte Order Mark (BOM) in the SOAP envelope when the envelope is correctly encoded using UTF-8 and the "charset" parameter of the HTTP Content-Type header has a value of "utf-8" (see RFC3023). CORE TESTABLE_SCENARIO_DEPENDENT BP1306

R4007.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT fault due to the presence of a UTF-16 Unicode Byte Order Mark (BOM) in the SOAP envelope when the envelope is correctly encoded using UTF-16 and the "charset" parameter of the HTTP Content-Type header has a value of "utf-16" (see RFC3023). CORE TESTABLE_SCENARIO_DEPENDENT BP1307

R1010.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT fault due to the presence of an XML Declaration in the SOAP envelope (as specified by Section 2.8 of� [XML1.0]," Prolog and Document Type Declaration ").

R1012.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST be serialized using either UTF-8 or UTF-16 character encoding.

R1018.statement: A SIMPLE_SOAP_MESSAGE MUST indicate the correct character encoding, using the "charset" parameter.

R1019.statement: A RECEIVER MUST ignore, if present, the encoding declaration of the envelope's XML declaration. CORE TESTABLE_SCENARIO_DEPENDENT BP1306

R1020.statement: A XOP_ENCODED_MESSAGE MUST include the start-info parameter in the Content-Type header of the enclosing multipart/related MIME entity body.

R1021.statement: A XOP_ENCODED_MESSAGE MUST include the full value of the type parameter from the root entity body part inside the start-info parameter of the enclosing multipart/related MIME entity body part's Content-Type header.

R1022.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT fault due to the action parameter of an XOP encoded message being included with the value of the start-info parameter inside the Content-Type header of the enclosing multipart/related MIME entity body. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R9980.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST conform to the structure specified in SOAP Version 1.2 Part 1, Section 5, "SOAP Envelope" (subject to amendment by the Profile).

R9981.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST have exactly zero or one child elements of the soap12:Body element.

R1014.statement: The children of the soap12:Body element in an ENVELOPE MUST be namespace qualified.

R1008.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST NOT contain a Document Type Declaration.

R1009.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST NOT contain Processing Instructions.

R1033.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST NOT contain the namespace declaration xmlns:xml="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace".

R1017.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT fault on the absence of the xsi:type attribute in envelopes, except in cases where this attribute is required to indicate a derived type (see XML Schema Part 1: Structures, Section 2.6.1). CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R1032.statement: The soap12:Envelope, soap12:Header, and soap12:Body elements in an ENVELOPE MUST NOT have attributes in the namespace "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope".

R1029.statement: Where the normal outcome of processing a SOAP envelope would have resulted in the transmission of a SOAP response, but rather a fault is generated instead, the RECEIVER MUST NOT transmit the non-faulting response. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R1107.statement: A RECEIVER MUST interpret a SOAP message as a Fault when the soap12:Body of the message has a single soap12:Fault child. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R1141.statement: When HTTP is used as the transport, a MESSAGE MUST be sent using either HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/1.0. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1140.statement: When HTTP is used as the transport, a MESSAGE SHOULD be sent using HTTP/1.1. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1109.statement: If present, the values of the following parameters - type, start-info, action, and boundary - on the Content-Type MIME header field-value in a request MESSAGE MUST be a quoted string. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1124.statement: An INSTANCE MUST use a 2xx HTTP status code on a response message that indicates the successful outcome of a HTTP Request. HTTP-TRANSPORT NOT_TESTABLE

R1111.statement: An INSTANCE SHOULD use a "200 OK" HTTP status code on a response message that contains an envelope that is not a fault. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1112.statement: An INSTANCE SHOULD use either a "200 OK" or "202 Accepted" HTTP status code for a response message that does not contain a SOAP envelope but indicates the successful outcome of a HTTP Request. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1130.statement: An INSTANCE MUST use the "307 Temporary Redirect" HTTP status code when redirecting a request to a different endpoint. HTTP-TRANSPORT NOT_TESTABLE

R1122.statement: An INSTANCE using Cookies SHOULD conform to RFC2965. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1121.statement: An INSTANCE SHOULD NOT require consumer support for Cookies in order to function correctly. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1202.statement: When a CONSUMER is non-addressable, a SOAP ENVELOPE, that is described by the output message of a WSDL operation supported by an INSTANCE, MUST be bound to a HTTP Response message. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1203.statement: When an INSTANCE is non-addressable, a SOAP ENVELOPE, that is described by the input message of a WSDL operation supported by the INSTANCE, MUST be bound to a HTTP Response message. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1204.statement: When an INSTANCE is non-addressable, a SOAP ENVELOPE, that is described by the output message of a WSDL operation supported by the INSTANCE, MUST be bound to a HTTP Request message. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1160.statement: A RECEIVER, for the purposes of comparison of URI values of information items defined by the SOAP 1.2 specification, MUST treat the computed absolute URI values as simple strings as defined in RFC3986 (see RFC3986, Section 6.2.1). CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R1040.statement: If an endpoint requires use of WS-Addressing by use of a wsam:Addressing policy assertion, an ENVELOPE sent by a SENDER MUST carry all required WS-Addressing SOAP headers.

R1041.statement: An ENVELOPE that is a MustUnderstand SOAP fault, sent from an endpoint that has a policy alternative containing the wsam:Addressing assertion attached to its WSDL endpoint subject, MUST NOT contain a NotUnderstood SOAP header block with the qname attribute value that identifies a WS-Addressing defined SOAP header block.

R1142.statement: An ENVELOPE that includes a wsa:Action SOAP header block and which is described using a WSDL 1.1 description MUST conform to WS-Addressing 1.0 - Metadata, Section 5.1.

R1144.statement: When the wsa:Action SOAP header block is present in an envelope, the value of the action parameter, if present, on the Content-Type MIME header of the MESSAGE MUST be an absolute URI that has the same value as the value of the wsa:Action header. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1035.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST use the http://www.w3.org/2005/08/addressing/soap/fault URI as the value for the wsa:Action SOAP header element, when present, for either of the SOAP 1.2 defined VersionMismatch and MustUnderstand faults.

R1143.statement: When a message contains multiple WS-Addressing SOAP header blocks with at least one of those header blocks containing a soap12:mustUnderstand='1' attribute, then a RECEIVER MUST honor all the WS-Addressing SOAP header blocks or none of them.

R1145.statement: If a SOAP envelope does not contain any WS-Addressing header blocks, or contains WS-Addressing header blocks that do not include any soap12:mustUnderstand="1" attributes, and the RECEIVER chooses to ignore them, then any response (normal or fault) SHOULD be transmitted. If it is transmitted then it is transmitted on the HTTP Response message (if available). HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1146.statement: A RECEIVER MUST transmit non-faulting responses to the endpoint referred to by the wsa:ReplyTo header or generate a fault instead (per R1029).

R1036.statement: Regardless of whether the wsa:ReplyTo or wsa:FaultTo SOAP headers appear in the incoming message, a RECEIVER that receives a SOAP envelope that generates either a SOAP MustUnderstand or VersionMismatch fault SHOULD transmit either fault. If it is transmitted, such a fault is transmitted on the HTTP Response message (if available). HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1147.statement: If a fault is generated, the RECEIVER SHOULD transmit the fault (per R1029).

R1161.statement: Other than those faults specified in R1036, faults in R1147 SHOULD be transmitted by the RECEIVER as specified in WS-Addressing 1.0 - Core, Section 3.4.

R1162.statement: When the wsa:FaultTo SOAP header exists, the RECEIVER MUST NOT transmit faults to the endpoint referred to by the wsa:ReplyTo header.

R1148.statement: If an error occurs when transmitting the fault in R1147, a RECEIVER MAY choose to send a fault related to this transmission error on the HTTP Response (if available). HTTP-TRANSPORT

R1163.statement: When applying the processing rules defined by WS-Addressing 1.0 � Core [WSAddrCore], Section 3.4, if a related message lacks a [message id] property, the RECEIVER MUST generate a wsa:MessageAddressingHeaderRequired fault.

R1149.statement: If a RECEIVER detects one of the error conditions specified in Section 6.4 of the Web Services Addressing 1.0 - SOAP Binding {WSAddrSoap], it MUST generate a fault using the [Code], [Subcode], and [Subsubcode] listed for that particular error condition.

R1152.statement: If an INSTANCE attempts to send a message to a non-anonymous [destination] URI then the message MUST be transmitted in the entity-body of an HTTP Request.

R1153.statement: Except in cases in which an instance exposes a WSDL description and its endpoint includes a wsdl:port that has been extended with a wsa:EndpointReference, a RECEIVER MUST NOT fault a SOAP request message due to the absence of the wsa:To header.

R1154.statement: When sending a request message to an endpoint which is specified by a WSDL 1.1 description in which the wsdl:port element has been extended with a wsa:EndpointReference, if the wsa:Action SOAP header block is present, the SENDER MUST populate the wsa:To and reference parameter SOAP headers of that request message with the values of the wsa:Address and wsa:ReferenceParameters elements (respectively) of the extending endpoint reference.

R1155.statement: When sending a request message to an endpoint which is specified by a WSDL 1.1 description in which the wsdl:port element has not been extended with a wsa:EndpointReference, if the wsa:Action SOAP header block is present, the SENDER MAY populate the wsa:To SOAP header of that request message with the value of the location attribute of the wsoap12:address extension element.

R1156.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, a policy that contains the wsam:Addressing assertion MUST be attached to either a wsdl:port, a wsdl:binding or a wsdl:binding/wsdl:operation. CORE NOT_TESTABLE_XPATH

R1157.statement: If a DESCRIPTION has a policy alternative containing the wsam:Addressing assertion attached to a wsdl:binding/wsdl:operation, then all of the wsdl:operation s within that wsdl:binding MUST also have a policy alternative containing the wsam:Addressing assertion attached to them. CORE NOT_TESTABLE_XPATH

R1158.statement: In a DESCRIPTION the effective policy for a given endpoint MUST NOT contain both the wsam:AnonymousResponses and wsam:NonAnonymousResponses assertions within a single policy alternative. CORE NOT_TESTABLE_XPATH

R0001.statement: Either an INSTANCE 's WSDL 1.1 description, its UDDI binding template, or both MUST be available to an authorized consumer upon request.

R2007.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST specify a non-empty location attribute on the wsdl:import element.

R2008.statement: A CONSUMER MAY, but need not, retrieve a WSDL description from the URI specified in the location attribute on a wsdl:import element.

R4005.statement: A DESCRIPTION SHOULD NOT contain the namespace declaration xmlns:xml="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace".

R4002.statement: A DESCRIPTION MAY include the Unicode Byte Order Mark (BOM).

R4003.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST use either UTF-8 or UTF-16 encoding.

R2005.statement: The targetNamespace attribute on the wsdl:definitions element of a description that is being imported MUST have same the value as the namespace attribute on the wsdl:import element in the importing DESCRIPTION.

R2025.statement: A DESCRIPTION containing WSDL extensions MUST NOT use them to contradict other requirements of the Profile. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2026.statement: A DESCRIPTION SHOULD NOT include extension elements with a wsdl:required attribute value of "true" on any WSDL construct (wsdl:binding, wsdl:portType, wsdl:message, wsdl:types or wsdl:import) that claims conformance to the Profile.

R2027.statement: If during the processing of a description, a consumer encounters a WSDL extension element that has a wsdl:required attribute with a boolean value of "true" that the consumer does not understand or cannot process, the CONSUMER MUST terminate processing. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2101.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST NOT use QName references to WSDL components in namespaces that have been neither imported, nor defined in the referring WSDL document.

R2102.statement: A QName reference to a Schema component in a DESCRIPTION MUST use the namespace defined in the targetNamespace attribute on the xsd:schema element, or to a namespace defined in the namespace attribute on an xsd:import element within the xsd:schema element.

R2105.statement: All xsd:schema elements contained in a wsdl:types element of a DESCRIPTION MUST have a targetNamespace attribute with a valid and non-null value, unless the xsd:schema element has xsd:import and/or xsd:annotation as its only child element(s).

R2110.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, declarations MUST NOT extend or restrict the soapenc:Array type.

R2111.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, declarations MUST NOT use wsdl:arrayType attribute in the type declaration.

R2112.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, elements SHOULD NOT be named using the convention ArrayOfXXX.

R2113.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST NOT include the soapenc:arrayType attribute.

R2114.statement: The target namespace for WSDL definitions and the target namespace for schema definitions in a DESCRIPTION MAY be the same.

R2115.statement: A DESCRIPTION SHOULD NOT contain multiple global element declarations that share the same qualified name.

R2116.statement: A DESCRIPTION SHOULD NOT contain multiple type definitions that share the same qualified name.

R2201.statement: A document-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST, in each of its wsoap12:body element(s), have at most one part listed in the parts attribute, if the parts attribute is specified.

R2210.statement: If a document-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION does not specify the parts attribute on a wsoap12:body element, the corresponding abstract wsdl:message MUST define zero or one wsdl:part s.

R2202.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MAY contain wsoap12:body element(s) that specify that zero parts form the soap12:Body.

R2203.statement: An rpc-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST refer, in its wsoap12:body element(s), only to wsdl:part element(s) that have been defined using the type attribute.

R2211.statement: An ENVELOPE described with an rpc-literal binding MUST NOT have the xsi:nil attribute with a value of "1" or "true" on the part accessors.

R2207.statement: A wsdl:message in a DESCRIPTION MAY contain wsdl:part s that use the elements attribute provided those wsdl:part s are not referred to by a wsoap12:body in an rpc-literal binding.

R2204.statement: A document-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST refer, in each of its wsoap12:body element(s), only to wsdl:part element(s) that have been defined using the element attribute.

R2208.statement: A binding in a DESCRIPTION MAY contain wsoap12:header element(s) that refer to wsdl:part s in the same wsdl:message that are referred to by its wsoap12:body element(s).

R2212.statement: An ENVELOPE described using an rpc-literal binding MUST contain exactly one part accessor element for each of the wsdl:part elements bound to the wsoap12:body element in the rpc-literal binding corresponding to the envelope.

R2213.statement: In a doc-literal description where the value of the parts attribute of wsoap12:body is an empty string, the corresponding ENVELOPE MUST have no element content in the soap12:Body element.

R2214.statement: In a rpc-literal description where the value of the parts attribute of wsoap12:body is an empty string, the corresponding ENVELOPE MUST have no part accessor elements.

R2205.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST refer, in each of its wsoap12:header, wsoap12:headerfault and wsoap12:fault elements, only to wsdl:part element(s) that have been defined using the element attribute.

R2209.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION SHOULD bind every wsdl:part of a wsdl:message in the wsdl:portType to which it refers to one of wsoap12:body, wsoap12:header, wsoap12:fault or wsoap12:headerfault.

R2301.statement: The order of the elements in the soap12:Body of an ENVELOPE MUST be the same as that of the wsdl:parts in the wsdl:message that describes it for each of the wsdl:part elements bound to the envelope's corresponding wsoap12:body element.

R2302.statement: A DESCRIPTION MAY use the parameterOrder attribute of an wsdl:operation element to indicate the return value and method signatures as a hint to code generators.

R2303.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST NOT use Solicit-Response and Notification type operations in a wsdl:portType definition.

R2304.statement: A wsdl:portType in a DESCRIPTION MUST have operations with distinct values for their name attributes.

R2305.statement: A wsdl:operation element child of a wsdl:portType element in a DESCRIPTION MUST be constructed so that the parameterOrder attribute, if present, omits at most 1 wsdl:part from the output message.

R2306.statement: A wsdl:message in a DESCRIPTION MUST NOT specify both type and element attributes on the same wsdl:part.

R2401.statement: A wsdl:binding element in a DESCRIPTION MUST use the SOAP 1.2 binding as defined in the WSDL 1.1 Binding Extension for SOAP 1.2.

R2702.statement: When HTTP is used, a wsdl:binding element in a DESCRIPTION MUST specify the HTTP transport protocol with SOAP binding. Specifically, the transport attribute of its wsoap12:binding child MUST have the value "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/http". HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2705.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST either be a rpc-literal binding or a document-literal binding.

R2706.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST use the value of "literal" for the use attribute in all wsoap12:body, wsoap12:fault, wsoap12:header and wsoap12:headerfault elements.

R2709.statement: A wsdl:portType in a DESCRIPTION MAY have zero or more wsdl:binding s that refer to it, defined in the same or other WSDL documents.

R2710.statement: The operations in a wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST result in operation signatures that are different from one another.

R2711.statement: A DESCRIPTION SHOULD NOT have more than one wsdl:port with the same value for the location attribute of the wsoap12:address element.

R2712.statement: A document-literal binding MUST be serialized as an ENVELOPE with a soap12:Body whose child element is an instance of the global element declaration referenced by the corresponding wsdl:message part.

R2714.statement: For one-way operations, an HTTP Response MESSAGE MAY contain an envelope. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2727.statement: For one-way operations, a CONSUMER MUST NOT interpret a successful HTTP Response status code (i.e., 2xx) to mean the message is valid or that the receiver would process it. HTTP-TRANSPORT NOT_TESTABLE

R2716.statement: A document-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST NOT have the namespace attribute specified on contained wsoap12:body, wsoap12:header, wsoap12:headerfault and wsoap12:fault elements.

R2717.statement: An rpc-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST have the namespace attribute specified, the value of which MUST be an absolute URI, on contained wsoap12:body elements.

R2726.statement: An rpc-literal binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST NOT have the namespace attribute specified on contained wsoap12:header, wsoap12:headerfault and wsoap12:fault elements.

R2718.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST have the same set of wsdl:operation s as the wsdl:portType to which it refers.

R2740.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION SHOULD contain a wsoap12:fault describing each known fault. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2741.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION SHOULD contain a wsoap12:headerfault describing each known header fault. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2742.statement: An ENVELOPE MAY contain a fault with a detail element that is not described by a wsoap12:fault element in the corresponding WSDL description. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2743.statement: An ENVELOPE MAY contain the details of a header processing related fault in a SOAP header block that is not described by a wsoap12:headerfault element in the corresponding WSDL description. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2724.statement: If an INSTANCE receives an envelope that is inconsistent with its WSDL description, it SHOULD generate a soap12:Fault with a faultcode of "Client", unless a "MustUnderstand" or "VersionMismatch" fault is generated.

R2725.statement: If an INSTANCE receives an envelope that is inconsistent with its WSDL description, it MUST check for "VersionMismatch", "MustUnderstand" and "Client" fault conditions in that order. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2729.statement: An ENVELOPE described with an rpc-literal binding that is a response MUST have a wrapper element whose name is the corresponding wsdl:operation name suffixed with the string "Response".

R2735.statement: An ENVELOPE described with an rpc-literal binding MUST place the part accessor elements for parameters and return value in no namespace.

R2755.statement: The part accessor elements in a MESSAGE described with an rpc-literal binding MUST have a local name of the same value as the name attribute of the corresponding wsdl:part element.

R2737.statement: An ENVELOPE described with an rpc-literal binding MUST namespace qualify the descendents of part accessor elements for the parameters and the return value, as defined by the schema in which the part accessor types are defined. CORE NOT_TESTABLE_XPATH

R2738.statement: An ENVELOPE MUST include all wsoap12:header s specified on a wsdl:input or wsdl:output of a wsdl:operation of a wsdl:binding that describes it.

R2739.statement: An ENVELOPE MAY contain SOAP header blocks that are not described in the wsdl:binding that describes it.

R2753.statement: An ENVELOPE containing SOAP header blocks that are not described in the appropriate wsdl:binding MAY have the mustUnderstand attribute on such SOAP header blocks set to '1'.

R2751.statement: The order of wsoap12:header elements in wsoap12:binding sections of a DESCRIPTION MUST be considered independent of the order of SOAP header blocks in the envelope. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2752.statement: An ENVELOPE MAY contain more than one instance of each SOAP header block for each wsoap12:header element in the appropriate child of wsoap12:binding in the corresponding description.

R2744.statement: If the action parameter on the HTTP Content-Type header is present in a MESSAGE, its value MUST be equal to the value of the soapAction attribute of the corresponding wsoap12:operation in the WSDL description, if this attribute is present and not empty. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2760.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT rely on the presence of� a SOAPAction HTTP header to correctly process amessage. HTTP-TRANSPORT NOT_TESTABLE

R2761.statement: A SENDER SHOULD NOT include the SOAPAction HTTP header. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2747.statement: A CONSUMER MUST understand and process all WSDL 1.1 SOAP Binding extension elements, irrespective of the presence or absence of the wsdl:required attribute on an extension element; and irrespective of the value of the wsdl:required attribute, when present. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2748.statement: A CONSUMER MUST NOT interpret the presence of the wsdl:required attribute on a wsoap12 extension element with a value of "false" to mean the extension element is optional in the envelopes generated from the WSDL description. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2756.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST NOT include the wsoap12:soapActionRequired attribute. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2759.statement: A CONSUMER MUST treat the absence of the wsoap12:soapActionRequired attribute as if it had a value of 'false'. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2758.statement: A MESSAGE MAY omit the action parameter from the Content-Type HTTP header field. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2757.statement: A RECEIVER MUST NOT fault due to the absence or presence of the action parameter on the HTTP Content-Type header field. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R2800.statement: A DESCRIPTION MAY contain any content validated against [xmlSchema-1].

R2801.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST use [xmlSchema-2]as the basis of user defined datatypes and structures.

R2900.statement: The value of the wsa:Action header block in an ENVELOPE MUST equal the value (either actual or computed) of the wsam:Action attribute for the corresponding WSDL element (wsdl:input, wsdl:output, or wsdl:fault) contained in the target wsdl:operation of the wsdl:portType.

R2901.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, the actual value of the wsam:Action attribute for the wsdl:input element contained in the target wsdl:operation of the wsdl:portType MUST be equal to the value of the soapAction attribute, if present, of the wsoap12:operation element contained in the target wsdl:operation of the wsdl:binding.

R2028.statement: A DESCRIPTION using the WSDL namespace (prefixed "wsdl" in this Profile) MUST be valid according to the XML Schema found at " http://ws-i.org/profiles/basic/1.1/wsdl-2004-08-24.xsd ".

R2029.statement: A DESCRIPTION using the WSDL SOAP binding namespace (prefixed "wsoap12" in this Profile) MUST be valid according to the XML Schema found at " http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap12/wsdl11soap12-20060302.xsd ".

R2001.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST only use the WSDL "import" statement to import another WSDL description.

R2803.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, the namespace attribute of the wsdl:import MUST NOT be a relative URI.

R2002.statement: To import XML Schema Definitions, a DESCRIPTION MUST use the XML Schema "import" statement.

R2003.statement: A DESCRIPTION MUST use the XML Schema "import" statement only within the xsd:schema element of the types section.

R2004.statement: In a DESCRIPTION the schemaLocation attribute of an xsd:import element MUST NOT resolve to any document whose root element is not "schema" from the namespace "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema".

R2009.statement: An XML Schema directly or indirectly imported by a DESCRIPTION MAY include the Unicode Byte Order Mark (BOM). CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2010.statement: An XML Schema directly or indirectly imported by a DESCRIPTION MUST use either UTF-8 or UTF-16 encoding.

R2011.statement: An XML Schema directly or indirectly imported by a DESCRIPTION MUST use version 1.0 of the eXtensible Markup Language W3C Recommendation.

R2022.statement: When they appear in a DESCRIPTION, wsdl:import elements MUST precede all other elements from the WSDL namespace except wsdl:documentation.

R2023.statement: When they appear in a DESCRIPTION, wsdl:types elements MUST precede all other elements from the WSDL namespace except wsdl:documentation and wsdl:import.

R2030.statement: In a DESCRIPTION the wsdl:documentation element MAY be present as the first child element of wsdl:import, wsdl:part and wsdl:definitions in addition to the elements cited in the WSDL 1.1 specification.

R2206.statement: A wsdl:message in a DESCRIPTION containing a wsdl:part that uses the element attribute MUST refer, in that attribute, to a global element declaration.

R2701.statement: The wsdl:binding element in a DESCRIPTION MUST be constructed so that its wsoap12:binding child element specifies the transport attribute.

R2179.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, a wsoap12:fault MUST specify the contents of the SOAP 1.2 fault Detail element. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R2720.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST use the part attribute with a schema type of "NMTOKEN" on all contained wsoap12:header and wsoap12:headerfault elements.

R2749.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST NOT use the parts attribute on contained wsoap12:header and wsoap12:headerfault elements.

R2721.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MUST have the name attribute specified on all contained wsoap12:fault elements.

R2754.statement: In a DESCRIPTION, the value of the name attribute on a wsoap12:fault element MUST match the value of the name attribute on its parent wsdl:fault element.

R2722.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION MAY specify the use attribute on contained wsoap12:fault elements.

R2723.statement: If in a wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION the use attribute on a contained wsoap12:fault element is present, its value MUST be "literal".

R2707.statement: A wsdl:binding in a DESCRIPTION that contains one or more wsoap12:body, wsoap12:fault, wsoap12:header or wsoap12:headerfault elements that do not specify the use attribute MUST be interpreted as though the value "literal" had been specified in each case. CORE NOT_TESTABLE

R3100.statement: REGDATA of type uddi:bindingTemplate representing a conformant INSTANCE MUST contain the uddi:accessPoint element.

R3002.statement: REGDATA of type uddi:tModel representing a conformant Web service type MUST use WSDL as the description language.

R3003.statement: REGDATA of type uddi:tModel representing a conformant Web service type MUST be categorized using the uddi:types taxonomy and a categorization of "wsdlSpec".

R3010.statement: REGDATA of type uddi:tModel representing a conformant Web service type MUST follow V1.08 of the UDDI Best Practice for Using WSDL in a UDDI Registry.

R3011.statement: The wsdl:binding that is referenced by REGDATA of type uddi:tModel MUST itself conform to the Profile.

R5000.statement: An INSTANCE MAY require the use of HTTPS. HTTP-TRANSPORT

R5001.statement: If an INSTANCE requires the use of HTTPS, the location attribute of the wsoap12:address element in its wsdl:port description MUST be a URI whose scheme is "https"; otherwise it MUST be a URI whose scheme is "http". HTTP-TRANSPORT

R5010.statement: An INSTANCE MAY require the use of HTTPS with mutual authentication. HTTP-TRANSPORT
